name: Tarifit (Riffian Berber)

ancestors.notes: Zenati Northern Berber; Tarifit is the principal Berber variety of the Rif (northern Morocco).
Spanish adstrate from the Spanish protectorate era and ongoing contact through the Spanish exclaves of Melilla and Ceuta on the Rif coast (Wikipedia, Tarifit: loanwords such as familiya 'family').

Arabic adstrate (Moroccan Darija and Classical/religious Arabic): Wikipedia (Tarifit, citing Kossmann & Mourigh 2020) estimates ~51.7% of Tarifit vocabulary (56.1% of nouns, 44.1% of verbs) is borrowed, chiefly from Arabic, plus Spanish and French.

notes: Tarifit / Riffian Berber, a Zenati Northern Berber language of the Rif region of northern Morocco (~1.2M speakers). Modelled here in the Berber Latin alphabet (the same convention family as kab.json/shy.json), the dominant script online and in most publications per Wikipedia; Tifinagh (official in Morocco since 2003) and Arabic script are also in use and not modelled here. VOWELS: a basic system of /i, u, a/ plus a lax central /ə/ (written e in the Latin convention, as in Kabyle/Shawiya); /i a u/ have lax allophones [ɪ æ ʊ] and, near pharyngealised consonants, pharyngealised allophones [ɪˤ ɑˤ ʊˤ] (not modelled as separate graphemes — this is allophony, not orthography). CONSONANTS follow Kossmann & Mourigh (2020) 'An introduction to Tarifiyt Berber (Nador, Morocco)' as summarised by Wikipedia: nasals /m n ŋ/; plosives with pharyngealised counterparts /p pˤ t tˤ tʃ k kːʷ q ʔ b d dˤ dʒ g gːʷ/; fricatives /f θ s sˤ ʃ ʃˤ ç x ħ β ð ðˤ z zˤ ʒ ɣ ʕ ɦ/; approximants /l lˤ j w/; flaps/trills /ɾ ɾˤ r rˤ/; most consonants have geminate counterparts except /ŋ, tʃ, ʔ/. The most distinctive Riffian feature relative to other Northern Berber varieties (Kabyle, Shawiya) is the correspondence of other dialects' /l/ to Riffian /r/ (traditionally written ř), and an r-vocalisation process producing diphthong-like sequences ([ɛa], [a~æ], [ɔa]) — not modelled here for lack of a specific orthographic convention sourced this session, so ř is mapped to plain /r/ pending that. Only the plain (non-pharyngealised) consonant series is populated in graphemes for now; the pharyngealised series and the emphatic/gemination alternations documented by Kossmann & Mourigh would need their own cited orthographic convention (dot-under letters, as in shy.json) before being added — left for a follow-up pass rather than guessed. Massive Arabic/Spanish/French lexical borrowing (Kossmann & Mourigh 2020, cited via Wikipedia) is recorded as adstrate ancestry, not as extra graphemes. WOLD GOLD CONVENTION: the benchmark gold for this spec is the WOLD (World Loanword Database) Tarifiyt Berber chapter, contributed by Maarten Kossmann (https://wold.clld.org/vocabulary/6, https://wold.clld.org/language/6). Kossmann's own field documentation on that page gives a four-column conversion table (his WOLD spelling / IPA / standard linguistic transcription / official Tarifiyt orthography per Lafkioui 1997) and states explicitly that 'the transcription system has been adapted to the technical and scientific context of the database' — i.e. WOLD is NOT the everyday Berber Latin alphabet already modelled above, it is Kossmann's own scholarly transliteration, mostly bare IPA plus a handful of ASCII-safe stand-ins for letters IPA fonts of the time lacked: ā=aː, ƀ=β, č=tʃ, ç=ɕ, đ=ð, ə=ə, ħ=ħ, š=ʃ, ŧ=θ, ž=ʒ, ǧ=dʒ (ǧǧ=geminate dʒː), ʔ=ʔ, ʕ=ʕ, and ř=r (trill) — all now added as extra graphemes alongside the everyday-orthography digraphs (th/dh/sh/gh/3/j/ng) they duplicate in IPA value, so the spec can consume either convention. ŋ and ɣ occur in the WOLD gold as bare IPA already (Kossmann's table does not list them because no substitution was needed) and are now mapped as identity graphemes. Kossmann's table also marks pharyngealisation on consonants and on the long vowel with a following apostrophe (d' l' r' s' t' z' ā') — but he uses U+2019 RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK for it, not ASCII apostrophe, and the o2i tokenizer strips U+2019 as punctuation (category Pf) before scoring. This is NOT modelled here. Measured against the full 1533-word wold gold: 349 words (22.8%) carry the mark (e.g. t't'řam -> tˤːram), and those words score PER 0.230 against PER 0.052 for the rest, contributing roughly 56% of the spec's remaining error mass. The gold target genuinely encodes the pharyngealisation, so this is a real uncorrected error source, not a normalisation artifact — fixing it needs the tokenizer to stop treating U+2019 as punctuation for this spec, which is engine behaviour requiring a full-board regression gate and is left for a follow-up rather than attempted here.
